...together they divided off fields and a house to settle Cheng. The other brothers were angry that he was buying goodwill, went to his door, and insulted him harshly. But Cheng had lived long among bandits and was used to fierce ways. When he heard of it he flew into a rage and said: "When I came home, not one of you was willing to give me so much as a room. Luckily Third Brother remembered that we are brothers, as close as hands and feet, and now you blame him for it. Do you mean to drive me out?" He threw stones at Xiao. Ren and Yi each came out with staves, seized Zhong and Xin, and thrashed them without number. Cheng did not wait for them to bring a lawsuit; he sued them first before the magistrate. The magistrate in turn sent someone to ask the advice of Youyu. Youyu, having no choice, went to call on him, but only bowed his head and said nothing, shedding tears. When pressed, he asked only for a fair judgment from the magistrate. The magistrate then ruled that Xiao and the others must each give up fields and property to Cheng, so that all seven shares were made equal.

From then on Ren and Yi, together with Cheng, loved and respected Youyu twice as much as before. Once, as they were chatting and laughing, the talk suddenly turned to the burial of their mother, and they all wept together. Cheng said in anger: "To be so unfeeling is to be a beast!" He then wished to open the grave and rebury her properly. Ren and Yi ran to tell Youyu. Youyu hurried home to talk him out of it, but Cheng would not listen and fixed a date

<summary>In the tale of Zeng Youyu, the hot-tempered brother Cheng, back from years among bandits, fights the brothers who had denied him a home and wins a court ruling that divides the family property into seven equal shares. Grief over their mother's improper burial then moves Cheng to plan her reburial against the gentle Youyu's advice.</summary>
<keywords>Pu Songling, Liaozhai Zhiyi, Strange Tales from a Chinese Studio, Zeng Youyu, Cheng, Xiao, Ren, Yi, Zhong, Xin, brotherly duty, family property, lawsuit, magistrate, reburial, filial piety</keywords>
